verdict.reasoning: Patient reports “a really bad headache, had it for about a day now… mainly on the left side… kind of throbbing… quite sensitive to light,” which supports a 1‑day left‑sided throbbing headache with photophobia.

She states onset was “ever since yesterday morning, since I woke up really,” describes it as throbbing that “sort of comes and goes… just kind of fades, so it's still there a little bit,” and says it “seems to be better” when lying down, supporting onset on waking yesterday, intermittent, never fully resolving, and improved when lying down.

Transcript: Doctor asks about position: “Is it worse when you lie flat, or when you bend forward?” Patient: “no, think I've generally been lying down, seems to be better that way,” indicating position does affect it (better lying down). For cough/sneeze: “Any problems if you cough or sneeze? … no,” so not worsened by cough/sneeze is correct, but “not worsened by position” contradicts the reported improvement with lying down.

Denials: visual change (“any problems with your eyes, or your eyesight? … no”), abnormal smells or tastes (anosmia/ageusia) (“Any abnormal smells or tastes? Patient: No.”), nausea/vomiting (“Any, any nausea, vomiting? … no”), fever/URI (“Have you had any other symptoms, like feeling feverish, , runny nose, sore ears? Patient: No”), focal neurological symptoms (“any problems with weakness, tingling, numbness in your arms or legs? Patient: No”), and skin changes (“Have you had any changes in your skin? Patient: No”). Fever is not measured but feeling feverish is denied, consistent with the claim.

No prior headaches: “normally, do you get any headaches? Patient: Uh, no not really, it's not something I've, ever had before.” Possible work stress trigger: “anything you've done recently might've, triggered it? Patient: … may have been a bit stressed out at work, that kind of thing.”

Past history: “Have you had any significant medical problems? Any hospital admissions, operations…? Patient: Uh, no, not recently, nothing.” No specific past medical or surgical conditions are reported, supporting no past history.

Medication: “Do you take any medication? Patient: Uh, no, just contraception. … Which contraception? Patient: Uh, Microgynon, pill. … When did you start that one? Patient: Uh, about six years ago.” This supports Microgynon OCP use for six years.
Acute medication: “What tablets have you been taking already, for it? Patient: Uh, just Paracetamol.” This supports use of paracetamol as needed for the headache.

Allergy: “I'm allergic to Aspirin, so I haven't been taking that. Doctor: What happens when you take Aspirin? Patient: Um, I just feel really sick.” This supports aspirin allergy with nausea/sickness.
Family history: “my mum had, uh, high blood pressure, and she's got a history of migraines.” This matches maternal hypertension and migraines.

Social history: “who do you live with at home? Patient: Uh, just with housemates, um, just friends.” Alcohol: “do you drink much alcohol day-to-day? Patient: … probably, you know, a few drinks at the weekend.” Tobacco/drugs: “And do you smoke? Patient: No. Do you take any other drugs of any sort? Patient: No.”

Assessment: New left‑sided headache with photophobia and no prior headaches. Doctor: “this headache is new to you, and you've, you've not had regular headaches before? Patient: Yeah. … it does, sound quite like a migraine, but obviously if you had no history of that, in the past.” No aura symptoms described. This supports likely first‑episode migraine without aura.

Transcript shows a recent BP check: “Have you had your blood pressure checked recently? Patient: Uh, I haven't actually, no. … Have you had it checked, when you've had the , repeat prescription done? Patient: Yeah, yeah, so uh, probably about six months ago.” The fact states “no recent blood pressure reading,” which conflicts with a reading about six months ago.

Plan: “What I would, suggest is, taking, uh, um, some anti-inflammatories, along with the Paracetamol.” Later: “that would be the first thing to do, is to take some anti-inflammatories along with the Paracetamol. Make sure you're really well hydrated.” Patient reiterates ibuprofen specifically: “I'll take some Ibuprofen and I'll um, hopefully, be a bit better.”

Safety‑netting: “if it isn't settling, or it's getting worse, or you get any other change in your headache. Um, or you're unwell with it, with a high temperature, then we would certainly need to speak to you… If you have a raised temperature or, your headache's just getting worse, or you develop any rashes or anything like that. Then we'd need to speak to you straight away.” This covers fever, rash, worsening/persistent headache, and change in headache (neurological concern).
Plan: “I would, try and arrange to get your blood pressure checked, if you haven't had it checked for a while.” This is advice to arrange a BP check.
Plan: “and, thing to do is to have a thermometer at home, so you can make sure that your temperature's OK.” This matches advising obtaining a home thermometer.

Plan: “if you're getting persistent, um, headaches, or headaches associated with your menstrual cycle, or certain things seem to trigger these headaches. Then, it, it would be worth, having a further discussion about it.” This supports arranging review if recurrent or menstrual‑linked headaches occur for migraine work‑up.
